reviewed_by: Codex focused review of integrated Butler Notebook, project, workspace, Library, chat and report journeys
reason: Retain prior project lifecycle, chat rewind, Notebook edit, transcript export, product knowledge, registry, and typed-action selections. Cover exact shared Library catalog and revision guards, browser-owned file selection and original-file download, reindex and removal, artifact retention, background exclusion, product-help discovery, and receipt parsing. Nine frontend files collect 106 cases for Butler browser handoffs, the workspace API client contract, and previous project/export behavior. Eight paired non-loopback LAN Library profiles cover cancellation, authenticated upload, original-byte download, revision guard, read-back, refresh, reconnect, removal, and retained artifact journey in addition to the prior 32 cases. Integrate upstream bulk chat actions: full-list selection, partial failure and retry, archive/restore, pin/flag, deletion confirmation, destination and product-help discovery, and compact toolbar geometry. Add its four Python, three frontend-file and eight paired LAN browser selections to the reviewed cumulative plan; duplicate Python tests are selected once. Add project-scoped workspace text-file listing, bounded read, hash-guarded create/edit/rename, browser-confirmed delete and byte-verified download; select its Python, browser handoff and eight paired LAN profiles. Retain the already reviewed Core chat setup responsiveness, MCP tool preparation, and stream lifecycle regressions from the concurrent main integration. This Notebook slice adds a current cell source-hash guard to Core and MCP execution, bounded recent-run discovery, and typed Butler execute and interrupt with Core run read-back. Four selected Python cases cover exact-source refusal, queued interruption, ordered replay, and mode-change coordination; the existing product-help and registry cases cover action discovery. The existing eight Notebook production-LAN browser profiles now exercise edit, exact execution, stale-hash refusal, ordered output, interrupt, refresh, and accessibility with the pinned runtime. Prior cumulative selections remain because this PR still contains those changes. Extend the selected workspace journey with browser-owned binary file selection, incremental SHA-256, directory identity and content preconditions, Core entry read-back, cancellation, folder create/rename/empty-delete, and production LAN UI verification. Select the affected Workspace API regressions, Butler tool routing, receipt parsing, browser component, exact API client header contract, and product-help discovery. Existing eight workspace LAN profiles now cover the expanded journey; no unrelated Playwright area is added. This resource slice adds kernel instance and generation reads, exact idle restart with worker acknowledgement, selected-environment package version reads, pinned installation with post-install verification, and a truthful no-kernel UI/API receipt. Two new Butler resource unit tests, the existing Host-consent service test, and the NotebookPanel component file cover target, grant, policy, readback, and UI status. The existing eight Notebook production-LAN profiles now install a synthetic local wheel offline through Butler, run it, restart the exact kernel, prove variables cleared, and refresh the visible result. A Docker restart regression ensures a missing current container reports unknown, then an authorized install mounts the persisted environment and treats the exact installed pin as a read-backed no-op. The restart and package-install unit cases also cover mutual exclusion while either resource change is in progress. Reconcile the parallel Notebook implementation by retaining the serialized kernel/package Core contract and the synthetic-wheel LAN journey. Keep the Settings assistant operation catalog and search terms, corrected to kernel_status and installed_package, and select its existing discovery regression. This file-index slice adds scoped Butler status/connect/remove actions, project-revision conflict checks, a browser-owned host SQLite picker, Core read-back and host-file retention. Three new Python cases cover tool discovery, direct MCP text and structured-result path privacy, and stale API/service revisions; existing product-help and registry cases verify guidance and inventory. The existing Butler component and typed-action files gain one case each for picker handoff, receipt parsing, cancellation and observed result. Eight new exact production LAN profiles exercise the selected-project index, cancellation, private host-path selection, refreshed Notebook discovery, removal and retained host file. The focused Chrome 390 Notebook resource rerun resolves an ENOSPC fixture failure from the earlier matrix. The concurrent manual Notebook file-index picker now waits for Core status, uses current project revisions and resets on project change. Select its HostFolderPicker and NotebookFileIndexSettings component files (seven cases), the already selected NotebookPanel file with one added project-switch case, and eight paired production-LAN manual Notebook file-index profiles. The manual journey verifies cancellation, exact saved revision, retained host file, refreshed discovery, bundle hash, accessibility and mobile width. Merge the concurrent linked-project handoff while retaining the stronger Notebook resource and private file-index contracts. Collect the exact selected layers again: 73 Python cases, 135 frontend cases and 72 Playwright entries. The selected project lifecycle journey covers linked folder cancellation, authenticated host selection, Core path and pending Host consent read-back, Files after refresh, and managed-project create regression. The Butler component case checks the saved-reply outcome for cancellation and creation, so the confirmation survives history reload. The linked-project CI mobile failure was a test navigation mismatch: compact workbench uses More > Workspace tools > Files after refresh. The selected paired LAN project-lifecycle test now follows that existing responsive route; all eight profiles remain selected for final acceptance. The linked-project retry exposed a true route selection race: adding the new project to the catalog had selected it before Core readback and navigation, then the source URL boundary reselected the old project and could abort Butler. Butler now adds without selecting and navigates only after the Core identity/path and Host policy readback. Select the WorkspaceContext recovery file and its no-selection regression alongside the existing Butler component and eight paired LAN project-lifecycle profiles. The merged LAN Chromium 320 run exposed a second UI rollback after Core creation and target-project loading: a stale source Workbench query update could navigate back using a render-captured relative path. Guard shared session query writes by the route project and navigate with an absolute pathname. Keep the existing eight paired LAN project-lifecycle entries as the focused browser regression for this route transition. Extend the selected Butler work with one project-bound report journey: paginate report/source discovery, create a fixed-ID draft, edit with a current revision, hand off final sign-off to the operator, and confirm browser-only PDF and sensitive bundle downloads. Select the two new Core report cases, one product-help retrieval case, the existing digest/Chroma/registry checks, the report editor component file, the existing Butler browser-action/parser component files, and eight permanent paired LAN profiles for the new end-to-end report journey. Keep the earlier selected journeys because this cumulative PR still changes the shared Butler gateway and browser action parser. Report draft creation uses a narrow authenticated route for fixed UUID reconciliation while generic report IDs remain server managed; selected report Core and paired LAN tests prove validation, replay, and readback. Exact report action names are added to indexed guidance; the selected retrieval case proves discovery. Large source catalogs and summary offsets are bounded and paged. Browser create errors now retain deterministic 4xx after exact-ID readback, while uncertain response replay still checks Core. The first desktop LAN report attempt exposed a browser-only settings-intent collision for an open sign-off request. The selected parser and Butler component checks now use that exact phrase; the paired LAN test will verify the full handoff. The second desktop LAN attempt reached finalization and both downloads, then Axe exposed preexisting Reports-page landmark names and a section-level ARIA misuse. The selected report LAN test keeps the final Axe gate after a narrow markup repair.
exclusions: No native source changed, so no native tests are selected. Unrelated Python, frontend and browser journeys are excluded. Terminal lifecycle, existing-project host-folder relinking, direct browser page control, evidence upload, report deletion and note-transform authoring, and specialized device and administration handoffs remain separate work. Browser profiles emulate mobile devices; physical Safari and the operating system final download save location are unavailable. Butler Knowledge may separately supply bounded Library excerpts; the Library control action sends metadata only. Library removal proves Core item absence and original artifact retention, but not every downstream index cache after cleanup failure. Bulk chat uses exact per-chat actions, not an atomic Butler bulk change. The Notebook LAN journey uses the bundled pinned Host runtime, synthetic Host consent, network disabled, and a local synthetic wheel. External registries, live network access, and Docker package installation are outside that selected LAN journey; a focused Docker service regression covers unknown package state after Core restart. The workspace LAN journey covers a browser-owned synthetic file picker and guarded folder changes; it cannot prove adoption by an external filesystem consumer. Directory identities are optimistic preconditions, not locks against external terminal writes. File-index host selection is intentionally confined to the requesting authenticated browser; the model receives configured state and project revision without the host path. Browser action outcomes are stored against the saved Butler reply for refresh, while the host file remains outside Core ownership. The Playwright matrix uses a synthetic SQLite index and no external filesystem crawler. The manual file-index journey uses synthetic host SQLite and browser emulation; it does not verify a physical mobile device or external index writer. Report PDF and bundle downloads were checked in emulated browsers; physical Safari and final operating-system save location remain unavailable.
